claim: The rule asserts sqlglot must be used wherever SQL text is parsed, tokenized, classified, split or rewritten, with no regexes, `.split()` or first-word checks on SQL text anywhere — while the same bullet list names `_mysql_parse_sql` as the only exception.
source_excerpt: **Use sqlglot wherever SQL text is parsed, tokenized, classified, split or rewritten.** One parser gives the guards and the runners one view of a statement in every dialect, so they cannot disagree about it.
verify_against: First-party SQL-handling code under src/sqllens/ (safety/, agent/tools/, connectors/)
verify_hint: Grep src/sqllens/ for regex/startswith/split-based SQL handling (e.g. `is_read_shaped`, `first_sql_keyword`, `_strip_leading_comments`, `RunSqlTool`) to find sites the universal 'wherever ... cannot disagree' wording excludes but that the rule does not list as exceptions
